findings.issue_text: Migration inserts legacy hosts with raw SQL, bypassing normalization; URLs or paths are stored verbatim and cannot match runtime URI host lookups
Migration crashes for a blank default embed_category because the join returns no rows and `[0]['id']` is dereferenced before the uncategorized fallback
Hosts containing ports are accepted and persisted, but runtime matching uses `URI(url).host` without the port, so those hosts can never be allowed
No uniqueness constraint or validation exists for host; duplicate hosts with different categories make `.first` select an unspecified category
Admin embeddable-host update and destroy actions dereference missing records, returning 500 instead of 404
Client sets `host.category` from a still-null categoryId after saving without a category, so the uncategorized category is not displayed until reload

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hosts containing ports are accepted and persisted, but runtime matching uses `URI(url).host` without the port, so those hosts can never be allowed

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. Looking at the diff, the EmbeddableHost model validates hosts with a regex that allows ports (:[0-9]{1,5}), and the before_validation strips http/https and paths but NOT ports. However, in the `record_for_host` method, it uses `uri.host` which returns only the hostname without the port. So if someone saves 'example.com:8080' as an embeddable host, the database stores 'example.com:8080', but when checking if a host is allowed via `host_allowed?`, it extracts just 'example.com' from the URL and compares it against 'example.com:8080', which won't match. This is a real bug where hosts with ports can be saved but will never actually allow embedding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No uniqueness constraint or validation exists for host; duplicate hosts with different categories make `.first` select an unspecified category

adjudication.rationale: The finding is valid. Looking at the diff, the EmbeddableHost model (app/models/embeddable_host.rb) has no uniqueness validation on the host field - only a format validation. The migration (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb) creates the table without a unique index on host. The record_for_host method uses `.first` which would return an arbitrary record if duplicates exist. In topic_embed.rb, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` is used to determine which category to post to, so duplicate hosts could cause posts to go to an unspecified category. This is a real defect in the data model.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client sets `host.category` from a still-null categoryId after saving without a category, so the uncategorized category is not displayed until reload

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the save action in embeddable-host.js.es6, after host.save(props) succeeds, it sets host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))). The categoryId is initialized to null (line 9) and only set when editing an existing host (line 26). For a new host where no category is explicitly selected, categoryId remains null, so Category.findById(null) would return undefined/null. However, the server-side code in embeddable_hosts_controller.rb sets category_id to uncategorized_category_id when blank, so the server returns the correct category_id but the client overwrites it with null. This is a real bug where the UI won't display the uncategorized category until reload.
